publications.title: Check the firm before you invest, FCA warns, as AI scams rise
publications.summary: A third (33%) of UK adults say they have seen an investment promotion in the past year that they believe used artificial intelligence (AI), new research from the FCA shows. Reports of investment fraud to Report Fraud that mention suspected use of AI have risen by nearly 400% in a year, up from 193 in 2024/25 to 956 in 2025/26. Investment fraud victims lost an average of £28,188 in 2025/26.Most people feel confident they could spot an AI investment scam, but that confidence is lower when a well-known person is involved. Almost two-thirds (62%) of adults say they could identify an investment scam that used AI. publications.title: Motor finance compensation scheme calculation
publications.summary: While preparing our response to the legal challenges to our motor finance redress scheme, we identified some errors in how we categorised a small group of loan agreements. This data informed the annual percentage rate (APR) adjustment we use in our calculation of compensation. We set this at 17% for agreements from 1 April 2014. Our initial work to understand the impact of the errors suggests that, if there is any impact, this would be less than 1 percentage point either side of 17%.While the potential impact on average compensation is small – less than £10 per agreement, on average – we recognise this affects the ongoing litigation.We properly informed those challenging the scheme. Two of those challengers are due to serve their expert evidence on Friday 27 November 2026.
